outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: The Challenge of Controlling Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
outline.description: This chapter introduces the current state of text-to-image diffusion models, their impressive capabilities, and the fundamental limitations regarding fine-grained control. It defines the two primary downstream tasks addressed in the paper (Subject-driven and Controllable generation) and critically analyzes existing finetuning strategies, highlighting the lack of principled methods to preserve pretrained semantics while adapting to new tasks.
subtopics: Overview of Large Text-to-Image Diffusion Models (Stable Diffusion, DALL-E 2, etc.)
The need for fine-grained control: Limitations of text-only prompts
Task Definition: Subject-driven Generation (DreamBooth context)
Task Definition: Controllable Generation (ControlNet context)
Analysis of Existing Finetuning Strategies (DreamBooth, LoRA, Adapters)
The Problem with Euclidean Distance: Why standard weight updates fail to preserve semantics
Desiderata for Effective Finetuning: Efficiency vs. Generability Preservation

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: The Hyperspherical Energy Principle in Neural Networks
outline.description: This chapter provides the theoretical foundation for the proposed method by explaining 'Hyperspherical Energy' and why it is a superior metric for measuring semantic preservation in neural networks compared to traditional Euclidean distance. It explores the geometric interpretation of neurons on a unit hypersphere.
subtopics: Introduction to Neuron Geometry: Weight vectors as points in high-dimensional space
Defining Hyperspherical Energy: Pairwise cosine similarities and uniformity on the unit sphere
Semantic Information in Angles vs. Magnitudes: Empirical evidence from autoencoder experiments
Why Euclidean Distance is Insufficient for Semantic Preservation
The Invariance Property: How orthogonal transformations preserve pairwise angles (Hyperspherical Energy)
Connecting Hyperspherical Energy to Generalization and Stability in Classification tasks

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT): Framework and Theorems
outline.description: This chapter formally defines the Orthogonal Finetuning method. It explains how learning a layer-shared orthogonal transformation matrix allows models to adapt to new tasks without altering their hyperspherical energy, thereby theoretically guaranteeing the preservation of pretrained semantic structures.
subtopics: The Core Hypothesis: Modifying semantics requires rotating neuron directions

outline.**The Mathematical Formulation:** $\\mat: **Key Insight:** The attainable minimum of hyperspherical energy difference is zero if weights differ only by rotation/reflection.
**Interpretation:** OFT adjusts the canonical coordinate system of neurons rather than changing vector magnitudes or arbitrary angles.

subtopics: Learning Layer-Shared Orthogonal Matrices
Replacing Standard Gradient Descent Update with Orthogonal Transformation
Guaranteeing Exact Initialization at Pretrained Weights
Achieving Determinant +1 or -1 (Rotation vs. Reflection)
Hardware Requirements: High-performance GPUs with CUDA core support
description: OFT is model-agnostic (works on Transformers, CNNs) but optimized for diffusion backbones.
subtopics: Application to Fully Connected Layers
Adapting to Transformer Attention Mechanisms (vs. LoRA)
Applicability to Convolutional Layers
Universality of Orthogonal Constraints across Architectures
